messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: `canary-traffic-surge` (policy: canary-healthcheck)
incident-bot: Symptoms: 5xx rate up (canary v2), p50 latency > 2000ms, error budget burn for route /generate, region us-west-2
incident-bot: Triggered at 2178005555. Pager: alice (oncall)

deploy-bot: Rolling release detected: canary v2 -> 2026-03-14T02:59Z by @sara-eng
deploy-bot: Release notes: change -> kv-cache prefetch size + aggressive batching

alice: Acked PD alert. I'm paged and joining the thread. grabbing logs + metrics now :coffee:

mike-sre: I see the spike. tailing logs from canary instances now. looks like KV cache miss storm after the change.

sara-eng: confirmed the release made a prefetch size change. It was supposed to reduce cold-startes but might be thrashing memory on canaries.

mike-sre: repro snippet from one canary pod:
```
OOM kill -> kvcache_reclaim_loop() -> high GC pauses -> 5xx proxy errors
``` 
mike-sre: Also seeing concurrent requests pile up at the router, queue latency ballooning.

alice: Customer impact? any production traffic hit or only canary bucket?

mike-sre: Canary bucket got 10% of traffic. That's ~1200 reqs/min. Error rate correlates with canary tag.

nisha-support: Support: we've had 4 customers open support tickets complaining about slow responses for generation endpoints in us-west. CS is prepping a statement.

sara-eng: Rollout paused in console. Attempting an automated rollback to v1 for canary group.

deploy-bot: Rollout pause confirmed. Triggering rollback: `rollback canary-group -> v1 (stable)`

deploy-bot: Rollback task started (task id: rb-20260314-0210)

mike-sre: While rollback runs, I'll route new sessions away from canary via traffic-split override.

mike-sre: Executing:
```
redwoodctl routing override set --route /generate --exclude-tag canary-v2 --region us-west-2
``` 
mike-sre: Override applied. New sessions should hit stable v1 within ~30s.

alice: Noting timeline and actions in incident doc. Severity set to S2 pending rollback success.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert acknowledged by alice at 2178005560. Escalation paused.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed at 2178005625. canary instances replaced with v1.

mike-sre: Observability check: 5xx rate down to baseline in us-west-2 within 45s post-rollback. p50 latency back to normal.

nisha-support: CS update sent to affected customers (batched). Message: "We observed degraded responses for a small subset of traffic due to a canary rollout; rollback completed and we are monitoring. Follow-up incoming." :white_check_mark:

sara-eng: Root cause initial hypothesis: aggressive KV prefetch increase exposed a cache eviction pattern on smaller canary hosts causing GC/oom waves. We'll run canary analysis and add safety caps to prefetch size.

alice: Good. For now: - rollback complete - traffic override removed? mike?

mike-sre: Removing override now:
```
redwoodctl routing override clear --route /generate --region us-west-2
```
mike-sre: Cleared at 2178005690. Normal routing resumed.

alice: Creating follow-up tickets:
- INC-20260314-001: Incident postmortem (owner: sara-eng)
- TASK-evict-2026: Add prefetch safeties + e2e canary test (owner: eng-runtime)
- COMM-2026: Customer follow-up draft (owner: nisha-support)

sara-eng: I'll own the postmortem. First draft in 24h, include experiment logs + canary config diff.

mike-sre: Any final checks before I hand off? metrics look stable for 10m.

alice: I'll keep monitoring for one more 30m window and then hand to next oncall. Current handoff ETA 2178007355 (approx 30m). If anything flares I'll reopen PD.

ryan-cto: Thanks team. Good quick rollback. Please include a clear rollback criteria in the postmortem - e.g., >1% 5xx or p50 > 1s sustained for 3m.

nisha-support: CS will send a personalized note to the 4 customers impacted once postmortem has the proposed fix ETA.

alice: Handoff note: I'm leaving the channel at 2178007355. Oncall followup: watch canary-release pipeline and routing metrics. Ping me if escalations.

incident-bot: Incident timeline recorded. Incident status: mitigated. Ticket INC-20260314-001 created.

alice: Closing thread here. Will update postmortem link once available. :v:
